Plot style of mortensor

Source: R/plot-style.R
mt_plot_style.Rd

The plots of mortensor share one layout: a minimal theme, observed values as small transparent points, fitted values as solid lines, forecast medians as dashed lines with light interval ribbons, and a dotted vertical line between the last observed and the first forecast year. Strata with ordered levels (such as deprivation quintiles Q1 to Q5) are coloured on a red-yellow-green scale, other strata (causes, regions, models) with distinct colours (12 distinct colours; more are interpolated).

Usage

theme_mortensor(base_size = 11, legend = "bottom")

mt_palette(n, type = c("ordered", "categorical"), reverse = FALSE)

scale_colour_mortensor(
  ...,
  type = c("ordered", "categorical"),
  reverse = FALSE
)

scale_fill_mortensor(..., type = c("ordered", "categorical"), reverse = FALSE)

Arguments

base_size

Base font size.

legend

Legend position.

n

Number of colours.

type

"ordered" (red to green) or "categorical".

reverse

Reverse the order of the colours.

...

Passed to ggplot2::discrete_scale().

Value

theme_mortensor(): a ggplot2 theme; the scales: ggplot2 scales; mt_palette(): a character vector of colours.

Details

  • theme_mortensor(): the theme (ggplot2::theme_minimal() with the legend at the bottom);

  • scale_colour_mortensor(), scale_fill_mortensor(): the colour scales, for your own plots of mortensor results;

  • mt_palette(): the colours themselves.

The ordered scale runs from red (first level) to green (last level), with a dark yellow in the middle that stays visible on white; reverse = TRUE turns it around. Which end is red is a decision about the data: with the Index of Multiple Deprivation, Q1 is the most deprived quintile.

Examples

mt_palette(5)
#> [1] "#D7191C" "#FDAE61" "#D9B526" "#A6D96A" "#1A9641"
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
  fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(lee_carter(), x), h = 10, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
  e <- life_expectancy(fc, at = 65)
  ggplot2::ggplot(e, ggplot2::aes(period, q0.5, colour = sex)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    scale_colour_mortensor(type = "categorical") +
    theme_mortensor()
}
